hypothesis: Already-selected broad-market leadership paper candidates that close in the top 15% of the decision-day range may be crowded/chased rather than cleaner leadership; a bounded 0.90x paper-notional haircut can improve allocation after the accepted rank, low-extension, high-volatility, and trend-persistence stack.
interpretation: Decision-day strong-close crowding did not clear Gate 4 after correctly scaling shares and PnL. The selected 0.90x haircut improved EV in all windows but lost aggregate PnL and regressed one window on PnL, so no policy is retained.

protocol_answers.1_alpha_hypothesis: candidate_pool/risk allocation: strong decision-day close-location is a crowding signal deserving a bounded paper notional haircut.
protocol_answers.2_past_similar_experiments: Broad-market price-floor, rank-notional, low-extension ret5, high-volatility, and positive-day trend persistence were accepted; close-location crowding was not previously tested.
protocol_answers.3_single_variable: Only decision_close_location threshold/scalar changes inside one notional-haircut field; eligibility, rank profile, low-extension, high-volatility, trend-persistence, hold, slots, and universe controls stay fixed.
protocol_answers.4_acceptance: Gate 4 requires positive aggregate EV/PnL, all 3 windows EV-positive, no EV/PnL regression windows, >=8 adjusted trades across all 3 windows, concentration guard, and <=0.5pp max drawdown worsening.
protocol_answers.5_reproducibility: Script, shared helper, tests, JSON artifact, log, ticket, markdown artifact, and JSONL identify windows, parameters, and metrics.

rejection_reason: Selected strong-close crowding haircut improved aggregate EV but reduced aggregate PnL and had one PnL-regressed window.

shared_adapter_parity.reason: Gate 4 failed; no shared broad-market policy or production adapter change is retained.
